project_type: Python PDF-to-HTML conversion workshop: renders Jinja2 HTML templates to PDF and structurally compares each render against an immutable reference PDF in corpus/ (SSIM, pixel-delta, text/column drift at 300 dpi).
build_system: uv (pyproject.toml + uv.lock). Use `uv add`, `uv sync`, `uv run`. A Makefile wraps the canonical commands. No compiled build step.
test_framework: pytest (pinned 9.1.1). Tests in tests/: test_catalog.py, test_evidence.py, test_fidelity.py, test_templates.py. pyproject sets addopts=-q, testpaths=[tests], pythonpath=[.]. test_fidelity.py reads committed output/*/report.json and asserts against unchanged THRESHOLDS; many cases are skipped when a report is still wip.
test_command: uv run pytest  (equivalently `make test`); `make check` runs `uv run ruff check .` then pytest.
verification_instructions: 1) `make setup` (installs poppler/pdftoppm and licensed Arial/Times via dnf+sourceforge; needs network; dnf and OPEN_INTERNET are available). 2) `make doctor` should print 'environment ready'. 3) Render a single report: `uv run python -m tools.render primary council_best_students`. 4) Compare: `uv run python -m tools.compare primary council_best_students` (requires pdftoppm). 5) Full loop for one report: `make convert-one LEVEL=primary REPORT=council_best_students`. 6) Whole corpus: `make convert` (long-running, 46 reports). 7) `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run pytest` must stay green. 8) Refresh README status table + sizes with `uv run python -m tools.status`.
snapshot_or_generated_files: output/<level>/<key>/{rendered.pdf, rendered-page-NN.png, diff-page-NN.png, report.json} are generated AND committed (a reviewer inspects the diff in the PR). Regenerate with `tools.render` + `tools.compare` (or `tools.convert`). README conversion-status table is generated by `tools/status.py` between the <!-- conversion-status:start/end --> markers. catalog/reports.yaml status field is updated by compare via tools/common.set_status. templates/_shared/fonts/report-*.otf are generated by `make fonts` (tools/fonts.py). corpus/ is READ-ONLY reference, never edited.
setup_instructions: cd /projects/sandbox/mussannoni; `uv sync` to install deps; `make setup` to install poppler + licensed fonts (dnf install poppler-utils liberation-*-fonts cabextract, then download Arial/Times from sourceforge corefonts). Confirm with `make doctor` -> 'environment ready'. weasyprint has already been added to pyproject via `uv add weasyprint` during routing (pyproject.toml and uv.lock are already modified in the working tree).
environment_constraints: OPEN_INTERNET (network available). dnf and yum present (Amazon Linux 2023). At session start: pdftoppm NOT installed, licensed Arial/Times NOT installed, weasyprint NOT importable (now added). agent-browser IS installed (Node CLI at ~/.nvm/.../bin/agent-browser) and is the current Chromium engine. NOTE: `import fitz` fails; the library is imported as `import pymupdf` (PyMuPDF 1.28) throughout the codebase. If `make setup` cannot install poppler/fonts in this sandbox, compare/SSIM metrics will differ from committed values; PDF-size verification via PyMuPDF does NOT need poppler and must still be done.
contribution_requirements: corpus/ is immutable and must never be edited. Fidelity THRESHOLDS in tools/compare.py and tests/test_fidelity.py must never be relaxed. Templates carry no literal sample data (test_templates.py enforces this). Naming is by report identity. output/ is committed so diffs are reviewable. Keep ruff clean (line-length 100, target py311) and pytest green.
key_patterns: tools/common.py holds path helpers (ROOT, find_report, output_dir, template_dir, reference_path, load_catalog, set_status, write_json). tools/render.py currently: loads fixture.json, renders template.html via Jinja2 to work/<level>/<key>/rendered.html, then shells `agent-browser --session <s> open|wait|pdf|close` to write output/.../rendered.pdf, and raises RuntimeError if the result isn't a %PDF-. tools/convert.py orchestrates extract->scaffold->render->tune->scaffold->render->compare and imports `from tools.render import render`. tools/compare.py hardcodes report.json field "engine": "chromium (headless, print-to-pdf)" at ~line 382 and rasterises both sides with pdftoppm. tools/doctor.py REQUIRED_BINARIES=("pdftoppm","agent-browser"). README.md 'Rendering engine' section ALREADY documents an intended two-engine design (chromium default + weasyprint) referencing a mussannoni/pdf.py that does not exist in this repo; align the real tools/ implementation to that documented intent.
root_cause_pdf_bloat: MEASURED during routing on output/primary/council-best-students/rendered.pdf: 1,574,866 bytes vs corpus original 185,490 (~8.5x). The compressed stream bytes are comparable (128KB vs 103KB); the bloat is 1.27MB of UNCOMPRESSED PDF object dictionaries across 11,401 objects with NO object streams (ObjStm) - agent-browser/Chromium emits every absolutely-positioned span/chunk/vector as a plaintext PDF object. The templates place one span per glyph-chunk so object counts are huge. FIX PROVEN: reopen with PyMuPDF and `doc.save(path, garbage=4, deflate=True, deflate_fonts=True, use_objstms=1, clean=True)` (optionally doc.subset_fonts() first) -> 1,574,866 -> ~318KB-324KB, PIXEL-IDENTICAL at 150 dpi and identical extracted text and identical page geometry. Same ~4.9-5x reduction verified on council-school-rank-in-grade (5.1MB->978KB) and region-kata-jumla (5.5MB->1.06MB). WeasyPrint renders the same council-best-students template to a valid 4-page 792x612 PDF at only 69,441 bytes (smaller than the original), so WeasyPrint both adds engine choice AND independently solves the size problem - but its layout engine differs from Chromium's, so its fidelity (SSIM/drift) must be re-measured with tools/compare.py, not assumed.
directory_structure: tools/ = the pipeline (fetch, extract, measure, scaffold, render, tune, compare, convert, status, doctor, fonts, grid, evidence, catalog, common). corpus/{primary,secondary}/*.pdf = 46 immutable reference PDFs + MANIFEST.json. extract/<level>/<key>/ = machine-read spans/rules/geometry/fonts + rasters + embedded-fonts/. templates/{_shared,<level>/<key>}/ = the product (template.html, report.css, bindings.yaml, fixture.json, per-report fonts/). output/<level>/<key>/ = committed rendered.pdf + report.json + diff pngs. catalog/ = reports.yaml (46 entries, status field), subjects.yaml, dedup.md. docs/ = approach/fidelity/geometry/fonts. tests/ = pytest suite. work/ = gitignored scratch.
